title: A lab of 12-month pointers and the CDC pointing months are different tasks
summary: CDC lists pointing to ask by about 15 months and pointing to show by about 18 months for most children, while a lab found sharing effects in 12-month-olds who already pointed.
body: The US checklist uses a three-quarters cutoff: pointing to ask or get help at 15 months, and pointing to show something interesting at 18 months. Liszkowski and colleagues studied 12-month-olds already reported to point, and found more points across trials when an adult shared the event. The lab shows a motive among infants who point, near the first birthday. It does not move the checklist's three-quarters ages earlier. The samples, the selection, and the question differ, so the months stay two different measures.
